extracted.intended_audience: scholars serving as proposal reviewers for the ASHE annual conference (including first-time and experienced reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for evaluating and submitting reviews of proposals for the Association for the Study of Higher Education (ASHE) annual conference, including best practices, conflict-of-interest rules, proposal types, and use of the conference portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensuring a Quality Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance and best practices intended to produce a high-quality review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Reviewer Guide contains instructions on how to navigate the system as well a variety of best practices for completing a quality review. (Section heading: 'Ensuring a Quality Review')

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes about Reviewing Proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic area covering specific considerations when reading and evaluating individual proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a standalone section in the Reviewer Guide — intended to provide reviewers with particular notes about what to watch for and how to approach proposal evaluation. (Section heading: 'Notes about Reviewing Proposals')

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteering and Assignments as a Reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural expectations for volunteering to review and how assignments are handled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Reviewer Guide includes information on volunteering and assignments as a reviewer; implies standards about accepting/declining assignments and managing reviewer workload. (Section heading: 'Volunteering and Assignments as a Reviewer')

rubrics_metrics.name: ASHE Conflict of Interest Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that reviewers follow ASHE's conflict of interest policy when deciding whether to review and when completing reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASHE Conflict of Interest Policy is a named component of the Reviewer Guide and must be followed when taking assignments and providing evaluations. (Section heading: 'ASHE Conflict of Interest Policy')

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Types (Individual Presentations and Session Submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that different proposal formats exist (e.g., individual presentations, session submissions) and may require different evaluative attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Reviewer Guide lists 'Proposal Types' and specifically 'Individual Presentations' and 'Session Submission' as distinct items, indicating reviewers should apply format-appropriate expectations. (Section headings: 'Proposal Types', 'Individual Presentations', 'Session Submission')

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criteria / Proposal Evaluation Criteria and Rating Process
rubrics_metrics.description: The formal criteria and rating process used to evaluate proposals for acceptance to the conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site references 'Review Criteria' and the Critique with Care session will 'review key features of the ASHE proposal evaluation criteria and rating process.' While the page does not reproduce the detailed criteria, it identifies this as the central rubric reviewers must follow. (Section heading: 'Review Criteria'; session objective quote)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading the Proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: How reviewers should read submitted proposals to form a fair, informed evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as a section in the Reviewer Guide ('Reading the Proposal') — signals guidance on reading order, attention to required components, and interpreting author claims before rating. (Section heading: 'Reading the Proposal')

rubrics_metrics.name: Completing the Reviewer Worksheet
rubrics_metrics.description: Completing the structured reviewer worksheet used in the portal to record evaluations and ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Reviewer Guide includes 'Completing the Reviewer Worksheet' and 'Submitting Your Review' as steps, indicating that reviewers must enter evaluations via the worksheet and follow worksheet-specific guidance in the portal. (Section headings: 'Completing the Reviewer Worksheet', 'Submitting Your Review')

rubrics_metrics.name: Navigating the Conference Portal and Reviewer Assignment Page
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural guidance for logging in, accessing assigned reviews, and navigating the reviewer assignment interface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Reviewer Guide lists 'Notes about using the ASHE Conference Portal', 'Logging in to Review Proposals', 'Accessing your Assigned Reviews', and 'Navigating The Reviewer Assignment Page' — these are required procedural steps for accessing materials and submitting reviews. (Section headings enumerated)

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Deadline and Timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete deadline by which reviews must be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit deadline on the page: 'Reviews are due on Monday, June 2nd at 3:00pm Mountain/Denver Time.' Reviewers are required to meet this timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of Constructive Feedback (Examples of Constructive vs. Unconstructive Reviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for constructive, reliable, and professional feedback contrasted with unconstructive or unreliable reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASHE provides a PDF resource with examples titled 'Examples of Constructive and Reliable & Unconstructive and Unreliable Reviews' (not real reviews). This resource illustrates exemplar and problematic reviews to model professional tone, actionable critique, reliability, and constructive suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique with Care — Best Practices and Core Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Session objectives describing what constitutes high-quality peer review practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives for the 'Critique with Care' session: (1) Share best practices in providing quality, reliable, and constructive feedback; (2) Review key features of the ASHE proposal evaluation criteria and rating process; (3) Discuss aspects of both exemplar and problematic reviews; (4) Provide a 15-minute 'how-to' session on navigating the Conference Portal. The session is aimed at both novice and experienced reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based and Scholarly Resources on Peer Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to consult research and scholarship about peer review reliability, bias, ethics, and best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists a 'References and Supplemental Reading on Peer Review Processes' with multiple scholarly citations (e.g., AAUP Handbook, research on reliability and bias, recommendations for transparency and replicability). Reviewers are encouraged to consult these sources to inform equitable and rigorous review practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples Resource Disclaimer (Non-Real Reviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarification that provided example reviews are illustrative and not actual submitted reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page states: 'These examples are not real reviews.' This guides reviewers to treat the examples as pedagogical models rather than real-case precedent or evidence about past decisions.
